nodes.name: Tally marks
nodes.desc: Incised counting marks on bone — Ishango, Lebombo.

nodes.name: Lunar calendar
nodes.desc: Tracking months by moon phases — sowing and festival timing.

nodes.name: Sexagesimal place-value
nodes.desc: Base-60 positional notation — the first place-value system.

nodes.name: Babylonian arithmetic
nodes.desc: Reciprocal tables, squares, quadratic problems — computational mathematics.

nodes.name: Land surveying
nodes.prereq: cuneiform OR hieroglyphic OR chinese_script OR mesoamerican_script
nodes.desc: Measuring and recording field boundaries — rope-stretchers, the 3-4-5 triangle.

nodes.name: Standardised weights
nodes.prereq: token_counting AND (proto_writing OR hieroglyphic OR chinese_script)
nodes.desc: State-issued weight standards — Indus cubical weights, Mesopotamian mina/shekel.

nodes.name: Civil solar calendar
nodes.prereq: calendar_lunar AND (cuneiform OR hieroglyphic OR chinese_script OR mesoamerican_script)
nodes.desc: 365-day administrative year decoupled from lunar months — Egypt.

nodes.name: Water clock
nodes.desc: Clepsydra — measuring time by regulated flow.

nodes.name: Systematic astronomical records
nodes.prereq: arithmetic_babylonian OR ((hieroglyphic OR chinese_script OR mesoamerican_script) AND calendar_lunar)
nodes.desc: Babylonian Astronomical Diaries — nightly observations for 700 years.
capabilities: the empirical base for Greek astronomy

nodes.name: Intercalated calendar
nodes.desc: Lunar months with inserted leap months to track the solar year — 19-year Metonic cycle.

nodes.name: Practical geometry
nodes.emerged: ~1,850 BCE Egypt (Moscow papyrus; Rhind ~1,550 BCE); ~1,800 BCE Old Babylonian Mesopotamia; later the Sulba Sutras (India) and Han Chinese classics
nodes.prereq: surveying AND (cuneiform OR hieroglyphic OR chinese_script OR mesoamerican_script)
nodes.desc: Area, volume, similar triangles — Thales measuring pyramids by shadow.

nodes.name: Axiomatic geometry
nodes.desc: Proof from stated axioms — Euclid. Knowledge that can be VERIFIED from the text alone.

nodes.name: Statics and simple machines
nodes.desc: Lever law, centre of gravity, buoyancy, screw — designed rather than trial-and-error machines.

nodes.name: Geometric astronomy
nodes.desc: Epicycles, the Almagest — predictive planetary models from geometry.
capabilities: the base for all astronomy until Kepler

nodes.name: Abacus
nodes.emerged: ~300 BCE Greece (Salamis counting board); Roman hand abacus; Chinese suanpan first illustrated 1436 CE (an earlier text attributed to ~190 CE is disputed)
nodes.desc: Counting board and bead frame — calculation without writing.

nodes.name: Alchemy
nodes.desc: Systematic transformation of substances with theory — Hellenistic Egypt, Han China. Distillation, sublimation.

nodes.name: Distillation
nodes.desc: Separating liquids by boiling and condensing — the alembic.

nodes.name: Astrolabe
nodes.desc: Analogue computer of the celestial sphere — time, latitude, star positions.

nodes.name: Gunpowder
nodes.desc: Saltpetre-sulphur-charcoal — incendiary, then propellant.

nodes.name: Saltpetre refining
nodes.desc: Leaching and recrystallising potassium nitrate — the bottleneck input.

nodes.name: Hindu-Arabic numerals
nodes.desc: Decimal place-value with zero — India ~500 CE, transmitted via al-Khwarizmi.

nodes.name: Algebra
nodes.emerged: 628 CE India (Brahmagupta); ~820 CE Baghdad (al-Khwarizmi); 1247–1303 CE China (Qin Jiushao, Li Ye, Zhu Shijie)
nodes.desc: Systematic solution of equations — al-Khwarizmi.

nodes.name: Trigonometry
nodes.desc: Sine, tangent, spherical trig — for astronomy and qibla.

nodes.name: Experimental optics
nodes.desc: Ibn al-Haytham — vision by reflected light, camera obscura, experimental method.
capabilities: experimental method as a stated procedure

nodes.name: Double-entry bookkeeping
nodes.desc: Every transaction as equal debit and credit — auditable capital.

nodes.name: Corned gunpowder
nodes.desc: Granulated powder — consistent burn, stronger, storable.

nodes.name: Heliocentric model
nodes.desc: Copernicus; Kepler's ellipses — predictive and simpler.

nodes.name: Telescope
nodes.desc: Two-lens refractor — Lippershey 1608, Galileo 1609.

nodes.name: Microscope
nodes.desc: Compound (Hooke) and single-lens (Leeuwenhoek) — microorganisms seen.

nodes.name: Classical mechanics
nodes.desc: Laws of motion and gravitation — Principia 1687. Prediction from equations.

nodes.name: Calculus
nodes.desc: Newton and Leibniz independently — rates and accumulation.

nodes.name: Barometer and air pump
nodes.desc: Torricelli 1643; Boyle's pump 1659 — air has weight, vacuum exists, the atmosphere pushes.
capabilities: the concept behind the atmospheric engine

nodes.name: Quantitative chemistry
nodes.desc: Lavoisier 1789 — conservation of mass, oxygen, elements. Chemistry as a science.

nodes.name: Industrial sulphuric acid
nodes.desc: Lead-chamber process 1746 — the workhorse acid; "a nation's industry measured by its sulphuric acid".

nodes.name: Synthetic soda
nodes.desc: Leblanc 1791; Solvay 1861 — alkali for glass, soap, textiles without plant ash.

nodes.name: Chlorine bleaching
nodes.desc: Bleaching in hours instead of months in the sun — Berthollet 1785, Tennant 1799.

nodes.name: Synthetic dye
nodes.desc: Perkin's mauve 1856 — coal tar to colour; the German chemical industry.

nodes.name: Synthetic ammonia
nodes.desc: Nitrogen from air, 1909-13 — fertiliser without guano; feeds half of humanity; explosives for the wars.

nodes.name: Dynamite
nodes.desc: Nobel 1867 — nitroglycerine stabilised; tunnels, mines, canals blasted.

nodes.name: Electromagnetism
nodes.emerged: 1800-1831 CE (Volta's battery 1800; Oersted 1820; Ampère; Faraday's induction 1831)
nodes.desc: Oersted 1820, Faraday 1831 — current makes magnetic fields and moving fields make current: the motor and the generator.

nodes.name: Petroleum refining
nodes.emerged: 1853-1859 CE (Łukasiewicz's kerosene 1853 and refinery 1856; Drake's well 1859)
nodes.desc: Drake 1859; fractional distillation — kerosene, then gasoline.

nodes.name: Photography
nodes.desc: Daguerre 1839; negative process 1841 — mechanical image record.

nodes.name: Theory of evolution
nodes.desc: Darwin-Wallace 1858 — natural selection. Two independent discoverers.

nodes.name: Vacuum tube
nodes.desc: Fleming diode 1904, de Forest triode 1906 — amplification and switching; electronics begins.

nodes.name: Quantum mechanics
nodes.prereq: electromagnetic_field_theory AND thermodynamics AND spectroscopy AND periodic_system AND radioactivity
nodes.desc: 1900-1927 — Planck, Bohr, Heisenberg, Schrödinger. Matter at atomic scale; the theory behind electronics and nuclear.

nodes.name: Controlled nuclear fission
nodes.desc: Discovery 1938; Chicago Pile 1942 — the controlled, self-sustaining chain reaction.

nodes.name: Genetics
nodes.desc: Mendel 1866 (ignored); rediscovered 1900; chromosome theory 1915.

nodes.name: DNA structure and molecular biology
nodes.desc: Watson-Crick-Franklin 1953 — the code; sequencing 1977; PCR 1983.

nodes.name: Recombinant DNA
nodes.desc: Cohen-Boyer 1973 — genes moved between organisms; insulin 1982; GM crops 1996.

nodes.name: Synthetic polymers
nodes.desc: Bakelite 1907; nylon 1935; polyethylene 1933 — materials designed from petroleum.

nodes.name: Atomic clock
nodes.desc: Caesium 1955 — time to a billionth of a second; the basis of GPS.

nodes.name: Relativity
nodes.desc: Special and general relativity — mass-energy equivalence, gravitation as spacetime curvature.

nodes.name: Laser
nodes.desc: Coherent light by stimulated emission — maser 1954, ruby laser 1960.

nodes.name: Applied superconductivity
nodes.desc: Zero-resistance conductors at cryogenic temperature — high-field magnets.

nodes.name: Controlled fusion research
nodes.desc: Magnetic and inertial confinement of fusion plasma — net energy not yet commercial.

nodes.name: Interplanetary probe
nodes.desc: Uncrewed spacecraft sent to other planets.

nodes.name: Space telescope
nodes.desc: Observatories above the atmosphere.

nodes.name: Polymerase chain reaction
nodes.desc: Amplifying DNA a billionfold.

nodes.name: Genome sequencing
nodes.emerged: 1986 automated sequencer; 1995 first bacterial genome; 2001-2003 human genome
nodes.desc: Reading complete DNA sequences.

nodes.name: Gene editing
nodes.desc: Programmable editing of DNA with CRISPR-Cas9.

nodes.name: Catalytic converter
nodes.desc: Exhaust catalysts removing pollutants.

nodes.name: Carbon capture
nodes.desc: Separating CO₂ from emissions and storing it.

nodes.name: Counting-rod arithmetic
nodes.emerged: ~400 BCE China (Warring States counting rods from a Chu tomb at Changsha); ~305 BCE Tsinghua bamboo-slip decimal multiplication table; Nine Chapters methods compiled in Han times
nodes.desc: Decimal place-value arithmetic with rods laid on a counting board, including negative numbers and systems of equations.
capabilities: decimal place-value calculation on a counting board (rod numerals, blank for zero)
root extraction and elimination for simultaneous linear problems (Nine Chapters methods)

nodes.name: Systematic mineralogy
nodes.emerged: 1546 CE (Agricola, De natura fossilium); 1758 CE (Cronstedt's blowpipe mineral analysis)
nodes.desc: Identifying minerals by their physical properties and by blowpipe and chemical tests.
capabilities: typing of unfamiliar mineral occurrences in observed land (physical properties, blowpipe and wet tests)

nodes.name: Probability and statistics
nodes.emerged: 1654-1812 CE (Pascal and Fermat 1654; Bernoulli's law of large numbers 1713; Laplace 1812)
nodes.desc: The mathematics of chance, and of drawing conclusions from counts and measurements.
capabilities: statistical analysis of counts and errors

nodes.name: Biological classification
nodes.desc: Naming and classifying living species in one orderly system.
capabilities: systematic naming and classification of species

nodes.name: Cell theory
nodes.desc: All living things are made of cells, and disease begins in cells.
capabilities: cells as the units of life

nodes.name: Electromagnetic field theory
nodes.desc: Electric and magnetic fields as one theory: light is an electromagnetic wave, and such waves can be made — the theory behind radio.

nodes.name: Organic chemistry
nodes.emerged: 1828-1865 CE (Wöhler's urea 1828; Liebig's analysis 1830s; Kekulé's structural theory 1858-65)
nodes.desc: The chemistry of carbon compounds — analysing, synthesising and drawing their structures.
capabilities: carbon compounds analysed, synthesised and drawn as structures

nodes.name: Periodic system of the elements
nodes.desc: Ordering the chemical elements by their properties, so that the gaps predict elements not yet found.

nodes.name: Spectroscopy
nodes.emerged: 1814-1860 CE (Fraunhofer's solar lines 1814; Kirchhoff and Bunsen's spectral analysis 1859-60)
nodes.desc: Identifying substances by the lines in their light — even the composition of the stars.

nodes.name: Stratigraphy and geological mapping
nodes.emerged: 1669 CE (Steno: superposition and original horizontality); 1815 CE (William Smith's geological map of England and Wales)
nodes.desc: Reading rock layers in order and mapping them, to tell which formations may hold coal, ore or oil.
capabilities: geological maps and the prospectivity of host formations

nodes.name: Thermodynamics
nodes.emerged: 1824-1877 CE (Carnot 1824; Joule 1840s; Clausius and Kelvin 1850-51; Boltzmann 1877)
nodes.desc: The laws of energy and entropy, which set the limits of every heat engine.

nodes.name: DNA sequencing
nodes.desc: Reading the order of the bases in a DNA molecule.

nodes.name: Geophysical prospecting
nodes.emerged: 1879 CE (Thalen's magnetic survey method for Swedish iron ore); 1912 CE (Schlumberger's electrical prospecting); 1915 CE (torsion-balance oil survey, Egbell); 1921 CE (first reflection-seismic field test, Oklahoma)
nodes.desc: Magnetic, electrical, gravity and seismic surveys that reveal structures hidden underground.
capabilities: magnetic, electrical, gravity and seismic surveys of concealed structures

nodes.name: Nuclear physics
nodes.emerged: 1932 CE (neutron; first artificial disintegration; D-D fusion 1934); 1938-1939 CE (fission discovered and explained)
nodes.desc: The structure of the atomic nucleus: isotopes, the neutron and the splitting of uranium.
capabilities: nuclear structure, isotopes (including deuterium), the neutron, artificial radioactivity, slow neutrons
fission of uranium and the role of U-235; fusion reactions of light nuclei

nodes.name: Radiation detection and counting
nodes.emerged: 1908-1911 CE (Geiger's counter); 1911 CE (Wilson's cloud chamber); 1928 CE (Geiger-Muller tube); 1948 CE (NaI(Tl) scintillator)
nodes.desc: Counters, cloud chambers and film badges that detect and measure radiation.
capabilities: counters, cloud chambers, film badges and scintillators

nodes.name: Radioactivity and radiochemistry
nodes.emerged: 1896 CE (Becquerel: rays from uranium salts); 1898 CE (polonium and radium, the Curies)
nodes.desc: Some elements give off rays as they change into others — radium and polonium are found.
capabilities: radioactivity - radium and polonium, alpha, beta and gamma rays, transmutation (Rutherford and Soddy)
radiation exposure harms living tissue (recognised from 1901 burns)

nodes.name: Radioisotope production
nodes.emerged: 1934 CE (artificial radioactivity; cyclotron-made isotopes); 1946 CE (first reactor-made isotope shipment, Oak Ridge)
nodes.desc: Making radioactive isotopes in accelerators and reactors for tracing, testing and sterilising.
capabilities: making radioisotopes by cyclotron or reactor irradiation (tracers, Co-60, Ir-192, Mo-99/Tc-99m)
industrial radiography, sterilisation and tracer methods

nodes.name: Radiometric prospecting
nodes.emerged: before 1949 CE (car-mounted Geiger-Muller surveys by the USGS for the AEC); 1958 CE (airborne radioactivity surveys established)
nodes.desc: Surveying the ground, on foot, by car or from the air, for the gamma rays of uranium and thorium.
capabilities: gamma-ray surveying - ground, car-borne and airborne mapping of uranium, thorium and potassium

nodes.name: Semiconductor physics
nodes.emerged: 1931 CE band theory of semiconductors (A. H. Wilson, Cambridge); 1938-1939 CE rectifier theory (Schottky, Mott); 1940 CE p-n junction and silicon photovoltaic effect (Ohl, Bell Labs)
nodes.desc: The band theory of solids and the junction between differently treated semiconductors.
capabilities: band theory of solids and the p-n junction
